name: LNK364DN-TL
title: LNK362, LNK363, LNK364 (LinkSwitch-XT): off-line switcher with 700 V MOSFET and ON/OFF control
summary: LinkSwitch-XT is a family of three off-line switcher ICs that put a 700 V power MOSFET and its controller on one die. Regulation is by ON/OFF cycle skipping: each 132 kHz cycle is either enabled or skipped depending on whether more than 49 µA flows into FEEDBACK, so no loop compensation is needed. The chip powers itself from the DRAIN pin through a high-voltage current source into a 0.1 µF BYPASS capacitor, jitters its frequency to lower EMI, and has cycle-by-cycle current limit, auto-restart and hysteretic thermal shutdown. LNK362, LNK363 and LNK364 differ in current limit and on-resistance, giving roughly 2.6 to 9 W of output depending on part and input; they come in DIP-8B, SMD-8B and SO-8C packages.
key_figures: 132 kHz typ (124 to 140 kHz), 9 kHz peak-peak jitter
5.5 W adapter / 9 W open frame at 230 VAC; 4 W / 6 W at 85-265 VAC
<300 mW at 265 VAC without bias winding; <50 mW with one

notes: The order code reads LNK, then the series number 362, 363 or 364, then the package letter (P plastic DIP, G plastic surface-mount DIP, D plastic SO-8), then the lead finish, then an optional -TL.
Lead finish N is RoHS compliant and halogen free. Finish G is also RoHS compliant and halogen free but is not recommended for new designs.
-TL is tape and reel: 1 k pieces minimum for the G package, 2.5 k pieces for the D package; it is not offered for the P package. Without a suffix the part ships in the standard configuration.

circuits.title: Clampless flyback converter with LNK362
circuits.description: The basic LinkSwitch-XT flyback with no primary clamp. The primary runs from the DC input to DRAIN; the secondary feeds the output through D1 into C1. When the output rises past the Zener VR1 plus the optocoupler LED drop, LED current flows and the phototransistor, collector on BYPASS and emitter on FEEDBACK, feeds current into FEEDBACK and skips cycles. R1 sits across the LED. C2 decouples BYPASS; no bias winding is used.

parts.note: P1-P2 primary, S1-S2 secondary; P2 and S1 dotted

circuits.title: Flyback converter with LNK363/4
circuits.description: The same flyback as the clampless one, built with LNK363 or LNK364 and an RCD clamp across the primary: D2 from DRAIN into the parallel pair R2 and C3, returning to the DC input, limits the turn-off spike.

parts.note: P1-P2 primary, S1-S2 secondary; P2 and S1 dotted

circuits.title: 2 W universal input CV adapter using LNK362
circuits.description: A 6.2 V ±7%, 322 mA constant-voltage adapter for 85-265 VAC with no primary clamp. RF1 is the fuse and inrush limiter and, with C1, L1, L2 and C2, forms a pi filter against differential noise; R1 damps the ringing of L1 and L2. D1 to D4 rectify. T1's primary (pins 4/5 to 3) drives DRAIN; its two shield windings each have one end on the bus and the other end open. The low current limit of LNK362 lets the primary's own capacitance absorb the leakage spike. D5 and C4 rectify and filter the output. The output is set by VR1, R2 and the LED of U2; above it, LED current pulls current into FEEDBACK until about 49 µA stops switching. R3 passes about 1 mA to bias VR1 near its test current; R2 trims the output for the Zener's step values, and a TL431 can replace VR1 for tighter tolerance. CY1 (100 pF) keeps touch current under 10 µA; with jitter and the shield windings the design passes conducted and radiated EMI with more than 10 dBµV margin. C3 is the only part the IC needs for its own supply.

parts.note: primary 4/5 to 3 (3 dotted), secondary 9 (dotted) to 8; SH1 and SH2 are the open ends of two shield windings whose other ends join pins 4/5

operation.text: There is no PWM loop. Inside are an oscillator, a feedback sense block, a 5.8 V regulator, BYPASS undervoltage lockout, over-temperature protection, frequency jitter, current limit, leading-edge blanking, auto-restart and the 700 V MOSFET. Each cycle either runs or is skipped.

The oscillator averages 132 kHz and produces both the clock that starts each cycle and the DCMAX signal. Its frequency is swept by about 9 kHz peak-peak at a 1.5 kHz rate to spread conducted EMI in both average and quasi-peak detection. To see the jitter, trigger the oscilloscope on the falling edge of the DRAIN; the period then moves between about 136.5 kHz and 127.5 kHz (Figure 4).

FEEDBACK is a low-impedance source follower held at 1.65 V (LNK362) or 1.63 V (LNK363 and LNK364). Once more than 49 µA flows into it, its logic output goes low. That output is sampled only on the rising clock edge: high means the MOSFET turns on for that cycle, low means the cycle is skipped. Changes later in the cycle have no effect.

Whenever the MOSFET is off, the regulator draws current from the DRAIN to charge the BYPASS capacitor to 5.8 V; while the MOSFET is on, the chip runs from that stored charge. The internal circuits use so little power that the DRAIN alone keeps the part running. 0.1 µF on BYPASS serves both as decoupling and as storage. A 6.3 V shunt clamps BYPASS when current is fed in from outside through a resistor, as from a bias winding, which brings no-load consumption under 50 mW.
The MOSFET is held off when BYPASS falls below 4.8 V, and switching resumes only once BYPASS has climbed back to 5.8 V.
When the die passes about 142 °C the MOSFET stops switching; it starts again after the die has cooled by 75 °C.

MOSFET current is sensed each cycle; reaching ILIMIT ends the on-time for that cycle. For tLEB after turn-on the comparator is blanked so the spike from capacitance and rectifier reverse recovery does not cut the pulse short.

An oscillator-clocked counter is cleared every time FEEDBACK is pulled high. If FEEDBACK goes about 40 ms without being pulled high, as with an overload, a shorted output or an open loop, switching stops for 800 ms, then tries again, repeating until the fault clears. This cuts delivered power by 95% during the fault.

KP below 1 is ripple current over peak primary current; above 1 it is MOSFET off-time over secondary diode conduction time. Because of the flux density limit, designs usually end up discontinuous, which allows fast rather than ultra-fast output diodes and lowers EMI.

Without a clamp, only the capacitance at the drain node limits the leakage spike, so peak drain voltage depends on the highest AC line, VOR, leakage energy and primary winding capacitance; the longer leakage ringing can raise EMI. For universal or 230 VAC-only inputs: use no clamp only up to 2.5 W output, with LNK362 and VOR ≤ 90 V; at 2 W or less wind a two-layer primary so its capacitance is 25 to 50 pF; from 2 to 2.5 W add a bias winding with a standard-recovery rectifier, which acts as the clamp and can also supply BYPASS through a resistor (this turns off the internal high-voltage source and lowers dissipation and no-load power); above 2.5 W fit an RCD or Zener clamp. Keep the worst-case peak drain voltage under BVDSS, ideally at 650 V or less. With 110 VAC-only inputs LNK363 may also run clampless, at some cost in EMI from more leakage ringing.
Where a clamp is used it is an RCD network or a Zener (about 200 V) plus diode across the primary, laid out with short paths to the transformer and the IC.

Cycle skipping can put audio-frequency energy into the transformer. Keep peak core flux density below 1500 gauss (150 mT) and dip-varnish the transformer; do not vacuum-impregnate it, which raises primary capacitance and losses. Higher flux is possible after listening tests on production samples. Z5U ceramic capacitors in a clamp can also sing; a film capacitor or another dielectric cures it.

Ground at one point, from the input filter capacitor to the SOURCE copper. Place the BYPASS capacitor right at BYPASS and SOURCE. Keep the loop of input capacitor, primary and IC small, and the clamp close to transformer and IC. The SOURCE copper under the IC is the heat sink: make it as large as possible. Connect the Y capacitor from the positive terminal of the primary input capacitor straight to the secondary return so surge current bypasses the IC; with a pi filter, put its inductor between the negative terminals of the input capacitors. Put the optocoupler near the IC with short primary traces, away from drain and clamp traces. Keep the secondary, output diode and output capacitor loop small, with heat-sinking copper at the diode, more of it on the quiet cathode than on the anode, since a big anode area raises radiated EMI.

Drain voltage: at the highest input and peak (overload) power VDS should stay at or below 650 V, 50 V under BVDSS. Drain current: at highest ambient, highest input and peak power, look for transformer saturation and leading-edge spikes at start-up and in steady state; the spike should be under ILIMIT(MIN) by the end of tLEB(MIN), and drain current always within its absolute maximum. Thermal: at full power, lowest input and highest ambient, the IC, transformer, diode and capacitors stay in rating; allowing for RDS(ON) spread, SOURCE pins at 105 °C or less at low line and full power.
